sentences.text: Heard Mr. S. Rahman, learned counsel for the petitioners.

Also heard Mr. M.P.
Goswami, learned APP appearing for the State.
Apprehending arrest in connection with Gauripur P.S. Case No. 447/2022 under sections 120(B)/420/412/34 IPC read with Section 4 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002

, the petitioners have filed this application under section 438 Cr.P.C.
Let the case diary be produced on 17.03.2023.
The learned counsel for the petitioner has prayed for interim bail, which is opposed by the learned APP.

On a query of the Court, the learned APP has obtained instruction from the I.O. that earlier being investigation was being conducted, amongst others, for offence under Section 4 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002.
However, after detailed order by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Dhubri, the provisions of Section 4 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 has been withdrawn.

In view of above, the FIR prima facie does not disclose ingredients of cheating, the Court is inclined to grant interim pre-arrest bail to the petitioners Page No.# 3/3 by providing that in the event of the arrest of the petitioners, namely, (1) Abdur Rahman Mollah, (2) Bablu Miah, (3) Yusuf Ali, and (4)
Taher Ali in connection with the aforesaid case, they shall be released on interim bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000/- each with one suitable surety of like amount to the satisfaction of the arresting officer.

The interim pre-arrest bail is granted on the following conditions:
1. The petitioners shall make themselves available to the police or any other investigating agency or Court in the present case as and when required.

2. The petitioners shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him Page No.# 1/3 vs The State Of Assam on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81371995/
2 from disclosing such facts to Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
They shall not, in any manner, try to overawe or influence or intimidate the prosecution witness.
3. The petitioners shall not obstruct the smooth progress of the investigation/trial.
4. The petitioners shall not misuse their liberty in any manner.

5. The petitioners shall appear before the I/O within 7 (seven) days from today,
failing which the interim protection granted to the petitioners would lapse on the 8th day of the order.
